assumptions: W4 of PLAN-0006: the Jira intake edge, built in-session by a single writer, in a new .warp/tracker_intake.py. The network is kept at arm's length so the substance is gate-tested offline: the intake LOGIC (resolve + draft + refuse) and the risky Jira field MAPPING (_jira_issue_to_item, ADF flatten) are mechanical and gate-tested over the FakeTracker + a fixture issue; only the actual HTTP (JiraCloudAdapter's urllib calls) is reference-wired (needs live Jira, not gate-run, token from a secrets ref never a raw credential). No template twin (not a validate/policy_check load dependency, same as the other tracker modules). A REVIEW-DRIVEN SECURITY FIX was applied to the reviewed code and re-reviewed: the first review found a front-matter injection (an untrusted ticket title emitted verbatim into the rendered YAML could inject a front-matter key line, e.g. hijack id/schema); fixed with _fm_safe which collapses every control character (ord < 32) and, via a second split()/join pass, every Unicode line separator (U+2028/U+2029/U+0085) to single spaces at both the draft boundary and every front-matter emission, so ticket content can only ever be a scalar VALUE not a structural KEY. Two independent adversarial reviews (the full pass on 4223f0b and a scoped re-review bound to this commit 58ad5ec) both PASS with 0 blocking; the re-review tried 10 attack families (title/body/labels/components/owner/tab/Unicode-line-separators, and injections of id/schema/owner/status/plan/work/protected_paths/human_approval/acceptance_criteria) and none injected a structural key or escalated any field.

The ticket report body is intentionally NOT sanitized (it is emitted after the closing --- as the human-readable report, not front matter); a fenced fake-spec in the body cannot hijack the front matter or produce a second parsed spec (confirmed). An informational note carried forward, out of scope for W4: PLAN-0006 prose says .warp/trackers.yaml while WARP-0601 ships .warp/trackers.json - W4 takes the config as an argument and never reads it from disk, so it is unaffected.
